content: Even when you stumble from the path, the footprint leaves a lesson in humility.
author: Japanese Proverbs
sourceWork: Michi wa fumihazushite mo — Zen Mountain Sayings
explanation: No pilgrim reaches the shrine without wandering down dead ends or losing footing on muddy switchbacks. The wanderings are not wasted time; they teach us where the rocks are slick and strip away the pride of thinking we have already arrived.
practicalInsight: Look back at a recent error not with self-condemnation, but as a mapmaker examining an unmarked turn.
reflectionPrompt: What detour or mistake in your past ended up teaching you the exact humility you needed for who you are today?
